doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Amy brings the LPs
summary: Amy fetches records and names labels and titles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So as the ‘60s progress, you’re touring a lot. You’re playing larger rooms and...

[RETURNS WITH AN ARMFUL OF LPs] A lot of duplicates, though. I just grabbed them. These are later. But Western Man, that was Atlantic. This is Columbia, Mose Goes. This is Mose In Your Ear, Atlantic, a live record. Here’s Hello There, Universe. These were later—Blue Note. This is Swingin’ Machine, Atlantic. This is early... I think this was before A Word From Mose...
I Love The Life I Live. Was that Columbia, Dad?
So this might have been the first on Atlantic. Here’s The Transfiguration of Hiram Brown. The notes are by Teo Macero.
We don’t need that. The Transfiguration of Hiram Brown, we don’t need...
We’re just showing the albums, Dad.
Yeah, we’re just showing them. Here’s the compilation from Prestige, Mose

Allison Sings. This is later, Atlantic, I’ve Been Doin’ Some Thinking. This is the one that has “Everybody Crying Mercy.” Then the other one we were talking about, The Word From Mose, which was all vocals. Then what about the one...I love that one... Oh, here’s Wild Man On The Loose. But I love that one... V-8 Ford Blues, Dad. When was that? Epic.

You know which one you don’t have here, is I Don’t Worry About A Thing. Which has a really nice cover, too. You’re out in the woods, Dad, looking up, your eyes are really blue. I Don’t Worry About A Thing—that’s got “Your Mind Is On Vacation” on it.
